The Hindu Vocabulary 

1. Strategic (Adjective)
Meaning: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
Hindi: रणनीतिक.
Synonyms: Planned, calculated, tactical, key.
Antonyms: Random, accidental.
Example: The database will help in strategic planning against IED threats.
Related Words: Strategy (noun).

2. Alleged (Adjective)
Meaning: Said, without proof, to have taken place or to have a specified illegal or undesirable quality.
Hindi: कथित, आरोपित.
Synonyms: Supposed, claimed, professed, reported.
Antonyms: Proven, confirmed.
Example: Charges regarding the alleged acceptance of illegal gratification.
Related Words: Allege (verb).

3. Beneficiaries (Noun)
Meaning: A person who derives advantage from something, especially a trust, will, or life insurance policy.
Hindi: लाभार्थी.
Synonyms: Recipients, heirs, payees.
Antonyms: Donors, benefactors.
Example: The beneficiaries of the land-for-jobs scam were identified.
Related Words: Benefit (noun).

4. Undocumented (Adjective)
Meaning: Not having the appropriate legal document or license.
Hindi: बिना दस्तावेज़ के (अवैध).
Synonyms: Illegal, unofficial, unrecorded.
Antonyms: Documented, legal, official.
Example: The plight of undocumented immigrants or citizens.
Related Words: Document (verb).

5. Marginalised (Adjective)
Meaning: (Of a person, group, or concept) treated as insignificant or peripheral.
Hindi: हाशिए पर, उपेक्षित.
Synonyms: Sidelined, alienated, excluded, neglected.
Antonyms: Empowered, included.
Example: The verification process often hits the marginalised sections hardest.
Related Words: Marginalise (verb).

6. Backdrop (Noun)
Meaning: The setting or background for a scene, event, or situation.
Hindi: पृष्ठभूमि.
Synonyms: Background, setting, context, scene.
Antonyms: Foreground.
Example: The game is played against the backdrop of a stadium crowd.
Related Words: N/A.

7. Consulate (Noun)
Meaning: The place or building in which a consul's duties are carried out.
Hindi: वाणिज्य दूतावास.
Synonyms: N/A.
Antonyms: N/A.
Example: The Taliban official may also oversee the Mumbai consulate.
Related Words: Consul (noun).

8. Vanishing (Adjective)
Meaning: Disappearing completely; ceasing to exist.
Hindi: गायब होता हुआ.
Synonyms: Disappearing, fading, evaporating.
Antonyms: Appearing, emerging.
Example: The mystery of the vanishing voters in Bengal.
Related Words: Vanish (verb).

9. Deployment (Noun)
Meaning: The movement of troops or equipment to a place or position for military action.
Hindi: तैनाती.
Synonyms: Positioning, stationing, placement.
Antonyms: Withdrawal.
Example: The deployment of the new missile system.
Related Words: Deploy (verb).

10. Capability (Noun)
Meaning: The power or ability to do something.
Hindi: क्षमता, सामर्थ्य.
Synonyms: Ability, capacity, potential, power.
Antonyms: Inability, incompetence.
Example: Demonstrating the defense capability of the nation.
Related Words: Capable (adjective).

📌 INTEGRATION OF PRINCELY STATE.

#Unionanditsterritories

🔸️ At the time of independence, India comprised two categories of political units, namely, the British provinces (under the direct rule of British government) and the princely states (under the rule of native princes but subject to the paramountcy of the British Crown). 

🔸️ The Indian Independence Act (1947) created two independent and separate dominions of India and Pakistan and gave three options to the princely states which are :-

• joining India, joining Pakistan or remaining independent. 

🔸️ Of the 552 princely states situated within the geographical boundaries of India, 549 joined India and the remaining 3 (Hyderabad, Junagarh and Kashmir) refused to join India.

🔸️ However, in course of time, they were also integrated with India–Hyderabad by means of police action, Junagarh by means of referendum and Kashmir by the Instrument of Accession.

📌 FAZL ALI COMMISSION.

#Unionanditsterritories

🔸️ The creation of Andhra state intensified the demand from other  regions for creation of states on linguistic basis. 

🔸️ This forced the Government of India to appoint (in December, 1953) a three- member States Reorganisation Commission under the chairmanship of Fazl Ali to re-examine the whole question. 

🔸️ Its other two members were K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru. It submitted its report in September 1955 and broadly accepted language as the basis of reorganisation of states. But, it rejected  the theory of ‘one language-one state’. 

🔸️ Its view was that the unity of India should be regarded as the primary consideration in any redrawing of the country’s political units.

📌 J.V.P COMMITTEE.

#Unionanditsterritories

🔸️ Dhar commission report created much resentment and led to the appointment of another Linguistic Provinces Committee by the Congress in December, 1948, itself to examine the whole question afresh. 

🔸️ It consisted of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallahbhai Patel and Pattabhi Sitaramayya and hence, was popularly known as JVP Committee.

🔸️ It submitted its report in April, 1949, and formally rejected language as the basis for reorganisation of states.

🔸️ However, in October, 1953, the Government of India was forced to create the first linguistic state, known as Andhra state, by separating the Telugu speaking areas from the Madras state. 

🔸️ This followed a prolonged popular agitation and the death of Potti  Sriramulu, a Congress person of standing, after a 56-day hunger strike for the cause.
